transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Lunaris Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Infra), Diana Ruiz (Product)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough): quick cost econ review; caching looks promising; need production trace; follow-up on spreadsheet and kv config.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - cost per token review, caching numbers samir put together, then open q's and next steps.
[00:12] Priya: yeah thanks. we've been seeing higher token churn than predicted, so mostly want to validate tokens/sec per dollar numbers and where caching can help.
[00:20] Samir: cool. quick note - our numbers assume your avg prompt is ~1.2k tokens and 30% repeated prefix across requests based on the sample trace you sent last week. if that's changed can you confirm?
[00:30] Priya: that's about right for chat history + doc context, maybe spikes to 5k in a handful of flows.
[00:38] Ethan: fetal note - infra can't accept latency > 400ms p95 for the assistant endpoint; that is product hard-req.
[00:46] Maya: perfect, we'll keep latency constraint in the model. Samir, can you walk through the tokens/sec per dollar table?
[00:52] Samir: yeah - so table at high level: baseline hosted variant (32-bit fp model) gives roughly 18k tokens/sec per $1 on the instance mix we used - that's raw throughput without caching. switching to 8-bit quantized variant improves to ~46k tokens/sec per $1; that's about 2.6x improvement.
[01:12] Diana: wait those numbers are tokens per second per dollar - can you also put that into cost per 1M tokens?
[01:18] Samir: sure - baseline was around $55 per 1M tokens, quantized ~ $21 per 1M tokens in our hosted price model assumptions. caveat: those assume steady-state batching of 16 and 80% GPU utilization.
[01:32] Priya: interesting. how much of that is from batching vs quantization vs caching?
[01:36] Samir: good question - our split in the spreadsheet is: batching contributed roughly 1.5x improvement (from tiny batch -> batch 16), quantization added ~1.8x on top, and prefix/KV caching (for your workload) gave an extra ~1.2-1.3x when hit-rate is ~40-50%. combined you can see 2.8x to 3.6x depending on hit-rate.
[01:58] Ethan: what do you mean by prefix caching? like full KV cache for tokens?
[02:02] Samir: prefix/KV cache means we cache computed key-value (KV) states for repeated prefixes - so when the model sees the same opening context we reuse the KV cache and avoid re-computing earlier layers. it's especially helpful for multi-turn with repeated system prompt or long doc contexts.
[02:18] Priya: our sample trace had about 42% repeated prefixes, maybe higher in helpdesk flows. so 40-50% hit-rate aligns.
[02:24] Maya: Samir, any observed latency penalty when caching? we worry about cache lookup cost adding jitter.
[02:30] Samir: negligible - cache lookup is microseconds on NVMe or in-memory; biggest latency source is memory transfer and kernel launch. caching actually reduces end-to-end latency for repeated-prefix flows because you skip recompute. caveat is cold-hit scenarios where we might add a small penalty for cache population but it's rare at scale.
[02:50] Diana: and batching - doesn't larger batching hurt p95?
[02:54] Samir: yes batching trades latency for throughput. batched 16 improved cost materially but raised p95 by ~30-50ms in our tests. with your 400ms p95 constraint we were still within budget at batch 16 for most inputs, but for short prompts (<200 tokens) burst lanes or hybrid config recommended.
[03:12] Priya: what's hybrid config?
[03:14] Samir: route low-latency small prompts to dedicated fast nodes with smaller batch sizes, route bulk/long requests to high-throughput pools. Redwood's smart routing can do policy-based routing with fallback.
[03:24] Ethan: are we looking at Dedicated for this POC? we haven't budgeted reserved capacity yet.
[03:28] Maya: current plan is hosted, but if we can't hit cost targets with caching+batching we can evaluate Dedicated pools which have better tokens/sec/$ at scale because you can tune kernel choices and packing more aggressively.
[03:40] Priya: do you have concrete dedicated numbers?
[03:42] Samir: yes - on Dedicated GPUs (A100-like equivalent) with aggressive kernel tuning we see up to ~95k tokens/sec per $1 on our quoted capacity mix; cost per 1M tokens could be down to ~$10 in a committed scenario, but that's with reserved monthly commit and sustained utilization.
[03:58] Priya: okay that's compelling but requires commit.
[04:02] Diana: can you show an example of where caching gave immediate wins? any real-world trace?
[04:06] Samir: I pulled a snippet from a retail customer: repeated 800-token product descriptions with similar system prompt - caching reduced compute by 48% and lowered cost per 1M tokens from $30 to $16 for that flow. I'll share anonymized logs after the call.
[04:20] Maya: noted. Priya, in your flows which endpoints are most repeated?
[04:24] Priya: helpdesk chat and onboarding wizard - both have repeated company policy preamble and are high QPS.
[04:30] Ethan: about batching - can we get an adaptive batching setup? sometimes QPS spikes and sometimes it's low.
[04:36] Samir: yes Redwood supports adaptive batching - it grows the batch up to a limit based on queue depth and latency targets. we can cap p95 impact by setting a max latency threshold, e.g., 250ms for the batch wait.
[04:48] Priya: ok - curious about memory footprint with big KV caches, any limits?
[04:52] Samir: KV cache memory grows with sequence length and cached prefix count. we set TTLs and evict LRU - in our POC config we estimated ~10-20GB per 100k active users with average 1k prefix lengths. exact numbers depend on activity and TTL.
[05:08] Ethan: that's doable. what's the expected cache hit-rate uplift if we increase TTL?
[05:12] Samir: increasing TTL from 30min to 2 hours can move hit-rate +8-12% in sessionized workloads; downside is more memory and potential staleness for dynamic context.
[05:22] Diana: any security or PII concerns with KV caching? we need to ensure sensitive tokens aren't persisted in plain storage.
[05:28] Maya: Redwood supports encryption at rest, KMS-backed keys, and optional in-memory-only caches for sensitive fields. we can also configure per-customer cache policies.
[05:36] Priya: good. can you show the numbers in the spreadsheet with different hit-rate columns?
[05:40] Samir: yes the sheet has columns for 20/40/60% hit rates and batching 4/8/16. for your baseline 42% hit and batch 16 we project cost per 1M tokens ~ $7.50 for quantized hosted model, assuming 80% utilization. that's down from $21 without caching.
[06:00] Priya: wow that's meaningful. are there any hidden infra costs or egress fees we should consider?
[06:06] Maya: egress usually small for text only, but if you do embedding heavy flows (we saw none in your trace) or multi-model pipelines, that can add. we'll include a sensitivity row in the spreadsheet.
[06:16] Ethan: about the business logic - for long docs we saw spikes to 5k tokens, does caching still help?
[06:20] Samir: caching helps if the long doc has repeated preamble or you chunk and reuse earlier chunks; otherwise less benefit. For pure one-off long generations batching/quantization matter more.
[06:34] Diana: one more question on accuracy tradeoffs with 8-bit quant - do you have regression numbers?
[06:38] Samir: yes we ran evals on your prompt set - avg pass@k delta was <1.5% for typical conversational tasks; for numeric reasoning tasks we saw slight regressions in a small subset. we recommend running your eval set; we'll add a quantized-variant row in the performance tab.
[06:56] Priya: we'll run the evals. also can we see a sample of the router policy config? we want to ensure deterministic behavior during spikes.
[07:02] Samir: I'll export a starter policy - it includes route by latency SLO, model tier, and region. I'll also include a canary rollout config so you can roll quantized variants gradually.
[07:12] Maya: ok to recap next steps - Maya send spreadsheet, Samir send kv config and router policy, Priya/Ethan run benchmark and evals, follow-up sync week after results. schedule tentative dedicated deep-dive if numbers off.
[07:24] Priya: sounds good. thanks both.
[07:28] Ethan: quick nit - can you add cost sensitivity to utilization in the sheet? e.g., 60/80/95% utilization rows?
[07:34] Maya: yes we'll add utilization sensitivity.
[07:36] Diana: thanks.
[07:38] Maya: thanks all, we'll email notes and artifacts.

[End]
